ܝܫܘܥ.n: Y'shua. Matthew 1:21 ties the name to the root “to make alive”: he will give life to his people.

ܐܠܗܐ.n: Elohim. The Syriac word is Alaha.

ܪܘܚܐ.n: Spirit, wind, or breath. With “of holiness,” the Ruach haKodesh.

ܒܝܬ.n: House of, or between, in compounds.

ܡܠܬܐ.n: Miltha: a word, a matter, the expression of someone. Murdock renders it “Word” in John 1.

ܟܢܫܐ.n: A crowd, or a synagogue assembly.

ܡܪܝܐ.n: Master YHWH. Marya stands where the Hebrew has the divine name.

ܟܐܦܐ.n: Keefa, a rock. The same word is Shimon’s name and the thing he is named for.

ܕܩܘܕܫܐ.n: Of holiness. With “spirit”: the Ruach haKodesh.

ܚܠܦ.n: Instead of, in exchange for, on behalf of.

ܒܪܢܫܐ.n: Son of man, a human being. As a title, the Son of man.

ܦܐܪܐ.n: Fruit. The same letters can be the verb “he fled.”

ܫܠܝܚܐ.n: One who is sent. Murdock refuses “apostle” and writes legate.

ܕܡܝܐ.n: Of the water. The same letters can mean “the price.”

ܕܡܘܬܐ.n: Likeness, image. Philippians 2:6, in the likeness of Elohim.

ܫܪܒܬܐ.n: A family, a generation, a narrative.

ܛܠܝܐ.n: A boy, a child, a servant.

ܢܚܐ.n: He makes alive. Murdock often writes “resuscitate” for this root.

ܕܓܠܐ.n: A lie, or he lied. Same letters in this text.

ܫܒܩ.n: He left, he forgave, he allowed.

ܥܠܡܝܢ.n: Ages. “For ever and ever” is l-alam 'almin.

ܥܡܢܘܐܝܠ.n: Ammanu'el. The verse interprets it: our Elohim with us.

ܚܛܘܦܝܐ.n: A thing snatched. Murdock: “no trespass,” where the Greek has harpagmon, a robbery.

ܦܚܡܐ.n: A match, an equal. Philippians 2:6, the equal of Elohim.

ܫܝܘܠ.n: The place of the dead. Murdock renders the gates of Sheol as “the gates of death.”

ܡܥܡܘܕܝܬܐ.n: A standing-up, a confirming. The English reads “immersion.”

ܙܩܝܦ.n: He raised up, he hung, he crucified.

ܣܘܢܩܢܢ.n: Matthew 6:11, the bread of our need. Not the Greek word “daily.”

ܛܠܝܬܐ.n: Talitha, the word already in the Greek of Mark 5:41.

ܩܘܡܝ.n: Arise, spoken to a woman or girl.

ܐܬܦܬܚ.n: Mark 7:34. The Greek transliterates this Aramaic word as ephphatha.

ܢܚܝܘܗܝ.n: He will make them live. Matthew 1:21.

ܐܓܢ.n: He tabernacled, he pitched his dwelling among us.

ܦܤܐ.n: A lot, as in casting lots.

ܥܒܪܐܝܬ.n: In the Hebrew tongue. In the first century this often means the Jewish Aramaic speech. Acts 26:14.

ܡܚܝܢܐ.n: Murdock’s “Vivifier.” The title he uses where Greek has Saviour, from the root “to make alive.”

ܡܘܗܒܬܐ.n: A gift. Acts 2:38, the gift of the Ruach haKodesh.

ܟܘܡܪܐ.n: A priest, often of the temple service.

ܫܪܐ.n: He loosed, he allowed, or he lodged.

ܥܡܕܘ.n: Stand, be confirmed. The English reads “be immersed.”

ܒܪܫܝܬ.n: John 1:1. The same opening as Genesis in the Peshitta: bereshit.

ܡܥܡܕ.n: The one who makes others stand. The English reads “immersing.”

ܘܒܠܥܕܘܗܝ.n: John 1:3. Apart from him, not even one thing was.

ܦܛܪܘܣ.n: Petros, the Greek form of the rock-name. The Peshitta’s own name is Keefa.

ܟܪܣܛܝܢܐ.n: One called by the name of the Mashiyach.

ܘܢܩܪܒܢ.g: and he will bring us near

ܢܘܕܥܟܘܢ.g: he will make known to you

ܢܘܕܥܘܢܟܘܢ.g: they will make known to you

ܠܚܡ.n: The second word of Beth-Lekhem, house of bread. The loaf itself is ܠܚܡܐ.

ܕܢܟܫܠ.g: that he should cause to stumble

ܘܢܡܝܬܘܢ.g: and they will put to death

ܕܝܕܥܬܗ.n: In 1 John 2:4 these same letters are the verb: that I know him.

ܡܠܟܗ.n: In Acts 25:12, sons of his counsel means his advisers.
